 proportions and use it to solve real-world problems.","Demonstrate understanding of proportional reasoning using mathematical connections among ratios, rates and proportions to solve daily problems simple and compound interest; depreciation; VAT, levies and commission; currency exchange and purchasing power; utility bills and tiered tariffs; health calculations such as BMI and dosage; sports statistics; and direct, inverse and inverse-square variation.","family":"number","section":{"no":5,"name":"Ratios, Rates and Proportions","strand":"Number for Everyday Life","from":12,"to":14},"outcomes":["Use percentages, ratios and rates to solve budgeting, sharing and inheritance problems.","Calculate simple and compound interest and reducing-balance depreciation.","Work with VAT, levies, commission, exchange rates and utility tariffs.","Apply rates and ratios to health measures (BMI, dosage) and to sports statistics.","Recognise and solve direct, inverse and inverse-square variation problems."],"keywords":["percentage","budget","partnership","inheritance","principal","interest rate","simple interest","compound interest","depreciation","reducing balance","VAT","levy","commission","exchange rate","purchasing power","tariff","unit charge","service charge","BMI","dosage","success rate","direct variation","inverse variation"],"notes":[{"title":"Percentages are ratios","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A percentage is a ratio out of 100: $35\\%=\\dfrac{35}{100}=0.35$."},{"k":"ul","items":["**Percentage of an amount:** $35\\%$ of GH₵2000 $=0.35\\times2000=$ GH₵700.","**Multipliers:** an increase of $r\\%$ multiplies by $1+\\dfrac{r}{100}$; a decrease of $r\\%$ multiplies by $1-\\dfrac{r}{100}$.","**Reverse percentage:** if a price **after** a 15% increase is GH₵690, the original is $\\dfrac{690}{1.15}=$ GH₵600 (divide by the multiplier, do **not** take 15% off)."]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Sharing profits, land and estates","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Partnerships share profits in the ratio of what each partner invested or agreed. A will may give fixed fractions to some people and share the rest in a ratio. Work in stages: take out the fixed parts first, then share the remainder."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Interest","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Simple and compound interest","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"For a principal $P$ at a rate of $r\\%$ per year for $n$ years:"},{"k":"math","tex":"\\text{simple interest } I=\\frac{P\\times r\\times n}{100}\\qquad A=P+I"},{"k":"math","tex":"\\text{compound amount } A=P\\left(1+\\frac{r}{100}\\right)^n"}]},{"k":"p","text":"**Simple interest** is paid on the original principal only, so it grows by the same amount each year. **Compound interest** is paid on the growing balance (\"interest on interest\"), so it grows faster."},{"k":"fig","id":"w14-interest","caption":"GH₵1000 at 10% a year: simple against compound interest."}],"figs":["w14-interest"]},{"title":"Depreciation","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Most equipment and vehicles lose value. With **reducing-balance** depreciation at $r\\%$ a year:"},{"k":"math","tex":"V=P\\left(1-\\frac{r}{100}\\right)^n"},{"k":"fig","id":"w14-dep","caption":"A car losing 20% of its value each year."}],"figs":["w14-dep"]},{"title":"Taxes, levies and commission","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**VAT** (value added tax) is a percentage added to the price of goods and services. Price including VAT $=$ price $\\times\\left(1+\\dfrac{r}{100}\\right)$.","**Levies** are extra percentage charges set by government. For example, Ghana's E-Levy on electronic money transfers was introduced in 2022 and abolished in 2025.","**Commission** is a percentage charged for a service, such as changing money or selling property."]},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Rates change","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Tax rates, levies, exchange rates and tariffs change with each budget or market day. Always use the rate given in the question, and check the current rate in real life."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Exchange rates","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"An exchange rate is a rate between currencies: \"1 USD $=$ GH₵10.20\". To change money, multiply or divide by the rate, then deal with any commission. **Purchasing power** compares what the same item costs in different countries once prices are converted into the same currency."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Utility bills","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Electricity and water are charged by the **unit** (kWh or m³), often with a **tiered tariff**: a lower rate for the first block of units and a higher rate after that, plus a fixed **service charge**."},{"k":"fig","id":"w14-tariff","caption":"A tiered electricity bill."}],"figs":["w14-tariff"]},{"title":"Health and sports","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"life","title":"Rates in health","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**Body mass index:** $\\text{BMI}=\\dfrac{\\text{mass in kg}}{(\\text{height in m})^2}$. Adult categories: under 18.5 underweight; 18.5–24.9 normal; 25–29.9 overweight; 30 or more obese.","**Dosage:** a dose of $d$ mg per kg per day for a patient of mass $m$ kg is $d\\times m$ mg per day, split into equal doses.","**Drip rate:** volume $\\div$ time, in mL per hour."]},{"k":"p","text":"These are calculations for learning; real doses are always decided by health professionals."}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w14-bmi","caption":"BMI categories with three example values."},{"k":"p","text":"In sport, a **success rate** is $\\dfrac{\\text{successes}}{\\text{attempts}}$, often given as a decimal or a percentage; a **win ratio** compares wins with losses or with games played."}],"figs":["w14-bmi"]},{"title":"Variation","blocks":[{"k":"table","head":["Type","Equation","Example"],"rows":[["direct","$y=kx$","cost and quantity"],["inverse","$y=\\dfrac kx$","workers and days"],["inverse square","$y=\\dfrac{k}{x^2}$","force and distance"]]},{"k":"p","text":"Find $k$ from one pair of values, then use the equation."}],"figs":[]}],"examples":[{"title":"Budget percentages","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A family's monthly budget is GH₵2000: 40% for food, 30% for rent and transport, and 30% for other needs. How much goes to food? If the budget rises by 15%, what is the new food allowance (same percentages)?"}],"steps":["Food $=40\\%\\times2000=0.4\\times2000=$ GH₵800.","New budget $=2000\\times1.15=$ GH₵2300.","New food allowance $=0.4\\times2300=$ GH₵920 (also $800\\times1.15$)."],"answer":"GH₵800; then GH₵920","figs":[]},{"title":"Partnerships, land and estates","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Two partners share a profit of GH₵50 000 in the ratio $2:3$. (b) A farmer divides 120 ha between two sons in the ratio $3:2$. (c) An estate of GH₵120 000 gives the widow $\\tfrac14$ and shares the rest among three children in the ratio $3:2:1$. Find each share."}],"steps":["(a) 5 parts: 1 part $=$ GH₵10 000, so GH₵20 000 and GH₵30 000.","(b) 5 parts: 1 part $=24$ ha, so 72 ha and 48 ha.","(c) Widow: $\\tfrac14\\times120\\,000=$ GH₵30 000. Remainder GH₵90 000 in 6 parts of GH₵15 000.","Children: GH₵45 000, GH₵30 000 and GH₵15 000. Check: $30+45+30+15=120$ thousand ✓."],"answer":"(a) GH₵20 000, GH₵30 000 (b) 72 ha, 48 ha (c) GH₵30 000; GH₵45 000, GH₵30 000, GH₵15 000","figs":[]},{"title":"Simple and compound interest","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"GH₵5000 is invested at 12% a year for 3 years. Find the amount with (a) simple interest (b) compound interest."}],"steps":["(a) $I=\\dfrac{5000\\times12\\times3}{100}=$ GH₵1800, so $A=$ GH₵6800.","(b) $A=5000\\times1.12^3=5000\\times1.404928=$ GH₵7024.64.","Compound interest earns $7024.64-6800=$ GH₵224.64 more, because each year's interest also earns interest."],"answer":"(a) GH₵6800 (b) GH₵7024.64","figs":[]},{"title":"Depreciation","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A taxi bought for GH₵80 000 depreciates by 20% a year on the reducing balance. Find its value after 3 years and the total loss in value."}],"steps":["Multiplier $=1-0.20=0.8$.","$V=80\\,000\\times0.8^3=80\\,000\\times0.512=$ GH₵40 960 (year by year: 64 000, 51 200, 40 960).","Loss $=80\\,000-40\\,960=$ GH₵39 040, which is 48.8% of the price."],"answer":"GH₵40 960; loss GH₵39 040","figs":[]},{"title":"VAT and a levy","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Assume a VAT rate of 15%. (a) An item costs GH₵400 before VAT. Find the price with VAT. (b) A receipt shows GH₵690 including VAT. Find the price before VAT. (c) Under a 1% transfer levy, what is charged on a GH₵500 transfer?"}],"steps":["(a) $400\\times1.15=$ GH₵460.","(b) Divide by the multiplier: $\\dfrac{690}{1.15}=$ GH₵600 (VAT $=$ GH₵90).","(c) $1\\%\\times500=$ GH₵5. (Ghana's E-Levy worked like this before it was abolished in 2025.)"],"answer":"(a) GH₵460 (b) GH₵600 (c) GH₵5","figs":[]},{"title":"Exchanging money","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) At 1 USD $=$ GH₵10.20, how many cedis is 50 USD? How many yen do you get for 200 USD?"}],"steps":["(a) $50\\times10.20=$ GH₵510.","(b) Commission $=2\\%\\times100=2$ USD, so the total is 102 USD.","(c) $200\\times132.5=26\\,500$ yen."],"answer":"(a) GH₵510 (b) 102 USD (c) 26 500 yen","figs":[]},{"title":"A utility bill","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A household uses 420 kWh in a month. Find the bill and the average cost per kWh."}],"steps":["First 300 kWh: $300\\times1.50=$ GH₵450.","Remaining 120 kWh: $120\\times2.10=$ GH₵252.","Bill $=450+252+12=$ GH₵714 (see the figure in the notes).","Average cost $=\\dfrac{714}{420}=$ GH₵1.70 per kWh."],"answer":"GH₵714; GH₵1.70 per kWh","figs":[]},{"title":"BMI and dosage","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Find the BMI of a woman 1.65 m tall with mass 68 kg, and of a teacher 1.73 m tall with mass 82 kg, and state their categories. Find each dose."}],"steps":["(a) Woman: $\\dfrac{68}{1.65^2}=\\dfrac{68}{2.7225}\\approx24.98$: normal, but very close to overweight.","Teacher: $\\dfrac{82}{1.73^2}=\\dfrac{82}{2.9929}\\approx27.4$: overweight.","(b) Daily dose $=25\\times70=1750$ mg; each dose $=\\dfrac{1750}{3}\\approx583$ mg."],"answer":"(a) 24.98 (normal), 27.4 (overweight) (b) about 583 mg","figs":[]},{"title":"Sports statistics","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) A footballer scores 3 of 5 penalties. Find the shooting percentage."}],"steps":["(a) $\\dfrac35=0.6$, that is 60%.","(b) Wins : losses $=60:40=3:2$; winning percentage $=\\dfrac{60}{100}=0.6=60\\%$.","(c) $\\dfrac{10}{15}\\approx0.667=66.7\\%$."],"answer":"(a) 0.6 (b) $3:2$, 60% (c) 66.7%","figs":[]},{"title":"Inverse-square variation","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The force $F$ on an object varies inversely as the square of its distance $d$ from a source. $F=16$ N when $d=2$ m. Find $F$ when $d=4$ m."}],"steps":["$F=\\dfrac{k}{d^2}$, so $16=\\dfrac{k}{4}$ and $k=64$.","When $d=4$: $F=\\dfrac{64}{16}=4$ N.","Doubling the distance divides the force by $2^2=4$."],"answer":"4 N","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Financial mathematics","items":["Increase by $r\\%$: $\\times\\left(1+\\tfrac{r}{100}\\right)$; decrease: $\\times\\left(1-\\tfrac{r}{100}\\right)$; reverse: divide.","Simple interest $I=\\dfrac{Prn}{100}$; compound $A=P\\left(1+\\tfrac{r}{100}\\right)^n$.","Depreciation $V=P\\left(1-\\tfrac{r}{100}\\right)^n$.","Exchange: multiply or divide by the rate, then add commission.","Tiered tariff: charge each block at its own rate, then add the service charge.","BMI $=\\dfrac{\\text{kg}}{\\text{m}^2}$; variation $y=kx$, $y=\\dfrac kx$, $y=\\dfrac{k}{x^2}$."]}],"quiz":[{"q":"40% of GH₵2000 is","options":["GH₵800","GH₵80","GH₵1200","GH₵500"],"correct":0,"explain":"$0.4\\times2000$."},{"q":"The simple interest on GH₵1000 at 10% a year for 3 years is","options":["GH₵300","GH₵331","GH₵1300","GH₵30"],"correct":0,"explain":"$\\tfrac{1000\\times10\\times3}{100}$."},{"q":"GH₵1000 at 10% compound interest for 2 years amounts to","options":["GH₵1210","GH₵1200","GH₵1100","GH₵1020"],"correct":0,"explain":"$1000\\times1.1^2$."},{"q":"A machine worth GH₵10 000 depreciates by 10% a year. (c) Compare with straight-line depreciation of GH₵3000 a year.","steps":["(a) $12\\,000\\times0.75^3=$ GH₵5062.50.","(b) Year 4: $5062.50\\times0.75\\approx$ GH₵3796.88; year 5: about GH₵2847.66. So after **5 years** it is first below GH₵3000.","(c) Straight-line: $12\\,000-3000n$ reaches GH₵3000 after 3 years and zero after 4. distance.","steps":["(a) **Direct:** $d=vt$; doubling the time doubles the distance.","(b) **Inverse:** $t=\\dfrac{d}{v}$; doubling the speed halves the time.","(c) **Inverse:** days <script type="application/json" id="pack-y2w15">{"year":2,"week":15,"id":"y2w15","title":"Sequences and Series I: Patterns and Arithmetic Progressions","subtitle":"Sequences and series; patterns from plane figures (triangular, square and cube numbers, matchstick patterns, Fibonacci); arithmetic (linear) sequences and the nth term; finding the first term and common difference from two terms; testing whether a number is a term; the sum of an arithmetic series, sigma notation and finding the number of terms.","family":"algebra","section":{"no":6,"name":"Patterns: Sequences and Series","strand":"Algebraic Reasoning","from":15,"to":17},"outcomes":["Describe and continue patterns made from plane figures and find a rule for them.","Recognise an arithmetic progression (AP) and find its common difference.","Find and use the nth term $U_n=a+(n-1)d$, including from two given terms.","Find the sum of an arithmetic series using $S_n=\\tfrac n2[2a+(n-1)d]$ or $S_n=\\tfrac n2(a+l)$.","Solve problems that require the number of terms or the first term of an AP."],"keywords":["sequence","term","series","finite","infinite","pattern","triangular numbers","square numbers","cube numbers","Fibonacci sequence","arithmetic progression","linear sequence","common difference","nth term","general term","last term","arithmetic series","sum","sigma notation","arithmetic mean"],"notes":[{"title":"Sequences and series","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **sequence** is an ordered list of numbers that follows a rule; each number is a **term**. We write $U_1$ for the first term, $U_2$ for the second, and $U_n$ for the **$n$th term** (the general term). A sequence may be **finite** (it stops) or **infinite** (it goes on for ever)."},{"k":"p","text":"A **series** is the **sum** of the terms of a sequence: the sequence $2,4,6,8$ gives the series $2+4+6+8=20$."},{"k":"box","kind":"life","title":"Patterns around us","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Patterns appear everywhere: the hexagonal cells of a honeycomb, the rings of a tree, the ripples on a pond, the spirals of a pineapple or a sunflower. Many of these spirals count in **Fibonacci numbers**: $1,1,2,3,5,8,13,\\dots$, where each term is the sum of the two before it ($U_{n}=U_{n-1}+U_{n-2}$)."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Patterns from figures","blocks":[{"k":"fig","id":"w15-figurate","caption":"Triangular, square and cube numbers."},{"k":"table","head":["Pattern","First terms","$n$th term"],"rows":[["triangular numbers","1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …","$\\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$"],["square numbers","1, 4, 9, 16, 25, …","$n^2$"],["cube numbers","1, 8, 27, 64, 125, …","$n^3$"]]},{"k":"p","text":"A pattern that grows by the **same amount** each time gives a **linear** sequence."},{"k":"fig","id":"w15-matches","caption":"Each new square adds 3 matches."}],"figs":["w15-figurate","w15-matches"]},{"title":"Arithmetic progressions","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Arithmetic progression (AP)","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"An **arithmetic progression** (linear sequence) is a sequence in which each term is found by **adding a fixed number** $d$, the **common difference**, to the term before:"},{"k":"math","tex":"a,\\ a+d,\\ a+2d,\\ a+3d,\\ \\dots\\qquad d=U_{n+1}-U_n"}]},{"k":"p","text":"The terms go up when $d>0$ and down when $d<0$. Because the first term has $0$ lots of $d$, the second $1$ lot, and so on:"},{"k":"math","tex":"U_n=a+(n-1)d"},{"k":"p","text":"This simplifies to $U_n=dn+(a-d)$: a **linear** expression in $n$. Plotted against $n$, the terms of an AP lie on a straight line with gradient $d$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w15-line","caption":"Terms of an AP lie on a straight line."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Using the nth term","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**Find a term:** substitute the value of $n$.","**Is $x$ a term?** Solve $U_n=x$; it is a term only if $n$ is a positive whole number.","**Given two terms:** write two equations, such as $a+2d=11$ and $a+7d=31$, and solve them simultaneously.","**Three terms in an AP:** the middle one is the mean of the other two, $b=\\dfrac{a+c}{2}$ (the **arithmetic mean**)."]}]}],"figs":["w15-line"]},{"title":"The sum of an arithmetic series","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Gauss is said to have added $1+2+\\dots+100$ in moments by pairing the first and last terms."},{"k":"fig","id":"w15-gauss","caption":"Writing the sum forwards and backwards."},{"k":"p","text":"Write $S_n=a+(a+d)+\\dots+l$ forwards and backwards and add: each of the $n$ columns adds to $a+l$, so $2S_n=n(a+l)$."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Sum of an AP","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"S_n=\\frac n2\\big[2a+(n-1)d\\big]\\qquad\\text{or}\\qquad S_n=\\frac n2\\,(a+l)"},{"k":"p","text":"where $l=a+(n-1)d$ is the last term."}]}],"figs":["w15-gauss"]},{"title":"Sigma notation","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"$\\displaystyle\\sum_{r=1}^{n}U_r$ means \"add the terms $U_1$ to $U_n$\". For example $\\displaystyle\\sum_{r=1}^{5}(2r+1)=3+5+7+9+11=35$."}],"figs":[]}],"examples":[{"title":"Patterns from figures","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Find the 10th triangular number and the 10th square number. (b) Write the next three terms of the Fibonacci sequence $1,1,2,3,5,8,\\dots$ (c) Show that the sum of two consecutive triangular numbers is a square number."}],"steps":["(a) $T_{10}=\\dfrac{10\\times11}{2}=55$ and $10^2=100$.","(b) $5+8=13$, $8+13=21$, $13+21=34$.","(c) $T_{n-1}+T_n=\\dfrac{(n-1)n}{2}+\\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}=\\dfrac{n(2n)}{2}=n^2$. For example $6+10=16$."],"answer":"(a) 55, 100 (b) 13, 21, 34 (c) $T_{n-1}+T_n=n^2$","figs":[]},{"title":"A matchstick pattern","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Matchsticks make a row of squares: 4, 7, 10, 13, … matches. (a) Find the rule. (b) How many matches make 50 squares? (c) Which pattern uses 100 matches?"}],"steps":["(a) Each square adds 3 matches: $a=4$, $d=3$, so $U_n=4+3(n-1)=3n+1$.","(b) $U_{50}=3(50)+1=151$ matches.","(c) $3n+1=100$ gives $n=33$: the 33rd pattern."],"answer":"(a) $3n+1$ (b) 151 (c) $n=33$","figs":[]},{"title":"Finding the nth term","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Find the $n$th term of $2,5,8,\\dots$ and the 6th term. (b) Find the 15th term of $-3,-1,1,3,\\dots$"}],"steps":["(a) $a=2$, $d=3$: $\\ U_n=2+3(n-1)=3n-1$, so $U_6=17$.","(b) $a=-3$, $d=-1-(-3)=2$.","$U_{15}=-3+(15-1)(2)=-3+28=25$."],"answer":"(a) $3n-1$; 17 (b) 25","figs":[]},{"title":"Fractions in an AP","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) An AP has first term $\\tfrac12$ and 10th term 9. Find the common difference. (b) Find the general term of $-\\tfrac12,\\ 2,\\ \\tfrac92,\\ \\dots$"}],"steps":["(a) $9=\\tfrac12+9d$, so $9d=\\tfrac{17}{2}$ and $d=\\tfrac{17}{18}$.","(b) $a=-\\tfrac12$ and $d=2-\\left(-\\tfrac12\\right)=\\tfrac52$.","$U_n=-\\tfrac12+\\tfrac52(n-1)=\\tfrac52n-3$."],"answer":"(a) $d=\\tfrac{17}{18}$ (b) $U_n=\\tfrac52n-3$","figs":[]},{"title":"Two terms given","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The 3rd term of an AP is 11 and the 8th term is 31. (a) Find $a$, $d$ and $U_n$. (b) Is 99 a term? Is 150?"}],"steps":["(a) $a+2d=11$ and $a+7d=31$. Subtract: $5d=20$, so $d=4$ and $a=3$.","$U_n=3+4(n-1)=4n-1$.","(b) $4n-1=99$ gives $n=25$: 99 is the 25th term.","$4n-1=150$ gives $n=37.75$, not a whole number, so 150 is **not** a term."],"answer":"(a) $a=3$, $d=4$, $U_n=4n-1$ (b) yes ($n=25$); no","figs":[]},{"title":"Sums of APs","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Find the sum of the first 50 terms of $1,3,5,7,\\dots$ (b) Find $S_{10}$ for $3,7,11,\\dots$ (c) Evaluate $\\displaystyle\\sum_{r=1}^{20}(2r+3)$."}],"steps":["(a) $a=1$, $d=2$: $\\ S_{50}=\\tfrac{50}{2}[2+49(2)]=25\\times100=2500$.","(b) $a=3$, $d=4$: $\\ S_{10}=5[6+9(4)]=5\\times42=210$.","(c) The terms are $5,7,\\dots,43$: an AP with $n=20$, $a=5$, $l=43$, so the sum is $\\tfrac{20}{2}(5+43)=480$."],"answer":"(a) 2500 (b) 210 (c) 480","figs":[]},{"title":"Sum from the last term","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Find the sum of $1+3.5+6+8.5+\\dots+101$."}],"steps":["$a=1$, $d=2.5$, last term $l=101$.","Number of terms: $1+(n-1)(2.5)=101$, so $n-1=40$ and $n=41$.","$S_{41}=\\tfrac{41}{2}(1+101)=41\\times51=2091$."],"answer":"2091","figs":[]},{"title":"A condition on the sums","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"An AP has first term 3, and the sum of its first 8 terms is twice the sum of its first 5 terms. Find the common difference."}],"steps":["$S_8=4(6+7d)$ and $S_5=\\tfrac52(6+4d)$.","$S_8=2S_5$: $\\ 4(6+7d)=5(6+4d)$.","$24+28d=30+20d$, so $8d=6$ and $d=\\tfrac34$."],"answer":"$d=\\tfrac34$","figs":[]},{"title":"How many terms?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"How many terms of $3+7+11+\\dots$ must be added to give 210?"}],"steps":["$\\tfrac n2[6+4(n-1)]=210$, so $n(2n+1)=210$.","$2n^2+n-210=0$, which factorises as $(2n+21)(n-10)=0$.","$n$ must be a positive whole number, so $n=10$ (check with the previous example: $S_{10}=210$ ✓)."],"answer":"10 terms","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Arithmetic progressions","items":["AP: add the common difference $d=U_{n+1}-U_n$ each time.","$n$th term $U_n=a+(n-1)d$, linear in $n$.","Two terms given: solve two equations for $a$ and $d$.","$S_n=\\tfrac n2[2a+(n-1)d]=\\tfrac n2(a+l)$.","Triangular $\\tfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$, square $n^2$, cube $n^3$; Fibonacci: add the previous two."]}],"quiz":[{"q":"The next term of $2, 6, 12, 20, 30, \\dots$ is","options":["42","40","36","50"],"correct":0,"explain":"The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, then 12."},{"q":"The 6th triangular number is","options":["21","15","36","28"],"correct":0,"explain":"$\\tfrac{6\\times7}{2}$."},{"q":"The common difference of $11,-1,-13,-25,\\dots$ is","options":["$-12$","$12$","$-10$","$-14$"],"correct":0,"explain":"$-1-11$."},{"q":"The $n$th term of $7,11,15,19,\\dots$ is","options":["$4n+3$","$4n+7$","$7n+4$","$3n+4$"],"correct":0,"explain":"$a=7$, $d=4$: $7+4(n-1)$."},{"q":"The 17th term of the AP with $a=5$ and $d=2$ is","options":["37","39","35","34"],"correct":0,"explain":"$5+16(2)$."},{"q":"Which number is a term of $U_n=5n-2$?","options":["48","50","47","52"],"correct":0,"explain":"$5n-2=48$ gives $n=10$."},{"q":"If $x$, 10, 16 are consecutive terms of an AP, then $x=$","options":["4","6","3","8"],"correct":0,"explain":"$10=\\tfrac{x+16}{2}$."},{"q":"The sum $1+2+3+\\dots+40$ is","options":["820","800","1640","410"],"correct":0,"explain":"$\\tfrac{40}{2}(1+40)$."},{"q":"The sum of the first 10 terms of $2,5,8,\\dots$ is","options":["155","150","29","310"],"correct":0,"explain":"$5[4+27]$."},{"q":"$\\displaystyle\\sum_{r=1}^{4}(3r-1)$ equals","options":["26","11","30","22"],"correct":0,"explain":"$2+5+8+11$."}],"exercise":[{"q":"Write the first five terms of the AP with first term 8 and common difference 7.","a":"8, 15, 22, 29, 36"},{"q":"Write the first five terms of the AP with first term 2 and common difference $-5$.","a":"2, $-3$, $-8$, $-13$, $-18$"},{"q":"Find the 10th and 19th terms of (a) $8,11,14,\\dots$ (b) $8,5,2,\\dots$","a":"(a) 35, 62 (b) $-19$, $-46$"},{"q":"Find the sum of the first 23 terms of $4,-3,-10,\\dots$","a":"$\\tfrac{23}{2}[8+22(-7)]=-1679$"},{"q":"An arithmetic series has first term 4 and common difference $\\tfrac12$. Find the sum of (a) the first 20 terms (b) the first 100 terms.","a":"(a) 175 (b) 2875"},{"q":"Find the sum of the arithmetic series with first term 1, common difference 3 and last term 100.","a":"34 terms; $17\\times101=1717$"},{"q":"The sum of the first 20 terms of an AP equals the sum of the first 22 terms. If $d=-2$, find the first term.","a":"$10(2a-38)=11(2a-42)$: $a=41$"},{"q":"The 5th term of an AP is 23 and the 12th term is 58. Find the first term, the common difference and the 30th term.","a":"$d=5$, $a=3$, $U_{30}=148$"},{"q":"How many multiples of 7 are there between 100 and 500, and what is their sum?","a":"105 to 497: 57 terms; sum $\\tfrac{57}{2}(105+497)=17\\,157$"},{"q":"A pattern of dots has 5, 9, 13, 17, … dots. Which pattern has 201 dots?","a":"$U_n=4n+1=201$: $n=50$"}],"theory":[{"q":"Derive the formula $S_n=\\tfrac n2[2a+(n-1)d]$ for the sum of the first $n$ terms of an AP.","steps":["Let the last term be $l=a+(n-1)d$. Write the sum forwards and backwards: $S_n=a+(a+d)+\\dots+(l-d)+l$ $S_n=l+(l-d)+\\dots+(a+d)+a$","Add term by term. Each of the $n$ pairs adds to $a+l$, so $2S_n=n(a+l)\\quad\\Rightarrow\\quad S_n=\\frac n2(a+l).$","Substituting $l=a+(n-1)d$ gives $S_n=\\dfrac n2\\big[2a+(n-1)d\\big]$."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"The sum of the first $n$ terms of a sequence is $S_n=n^2+4n$. (a) Find $S_1$, $S_2$ and $S_3$. (b) Find the first three terms and show that the sequence is an AP. (c) Find $U_n$.","steps":["(a) $S_1=5$, $S_2=12$, $S_3=21$.","(b) $U_1=S_1=5$, $U_2=S_2-S_1=7$, $U_3=S_3-S_2=9$. The differences are both 2, so it is an AP with $a=5$, $d=2$.","(c) $U_n=S_n-S_{n-1}=(n^2+4n)-[(n-1)^2+4(n-1)]=2n+3$. Check: $U_1=5$ ✓."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Three numbers in an AP add up to 24 and their product is 440. Find the numbers.","steps":["Let the numbers be $a-d$, $a$, $a+d$. Their sum is $3a=24$, so $a=8$.","Product: $(8-d)(8)(8+d)=440$, so $64-d^2=55$ and $d^2=9$, $d=\\pm3$.","The numbers are **5, 8, 11** (or 11, 8, 5). Check: $5+8+11=24$ and $5\\times8\\times11=440$ ✓."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"A matchstick pattern of triangles in a row uses 3, 5, 7, 9, … matches. (a) Find the rule. (b) How many matches are needed for the first 20 patterns altogether? (c) With 500 matches, what is the largest single pattern you can make?","steps":["(a) $a=3$, $d=2$: $U_n=3+2(n-1)=2n+1$.","(b) $S_{20}=\\tfrac{20}{2}(3+41)=440$ matches.","(c) $2n+1\\le500$ gives $n\\le249.5$, so the largest pattern is $n=249$, using 499 matches."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Explain why the terms of an AP lie on a straight line when plotted against $n$, and say what the gradient and intercept of that line represent.","steps":["$U_n=a+(n-1)d=dn+(a-d)$. This has the form $y=mx+c$ with $x=n$, $y=U_n$, $m=d$ and $c=a-d$.","So the points $(n,U_n)$ lie on a straight line whose **gradient is the common difference** $d$ (the term rises by $d$ for each step in $n$) and whose **intercept** $a-d$ is the \"zeroth term\", the value one step before the first term. The terms are only the points at whole-number $n$, so the line is drawn dashed."],"answer":"","model":null}],"checklist":["I can tell a sequence from a series and continue patterns from figures.","I the other to remove $a$. For example $ar=9$ and $ar^3=4$ give $r^2=\\tfrac49$.","**Three terms in a GP:** the middle term $b$ satisfies $b^2=ac$; $\\ b=\\pm\\sqrt{ac}$ is the **geometric mean** of $a$ and $c$.","**Number of terms:** solve $ar^{n-1}=l$. When the power is not obvious, take logarithms (Week 2): $\\ n-1=\\dfrac{\\log(l/a)}{\\log r}$."]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Sum of a geometric series","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Write $S_n=a+ar+\\dots+ar^{n-1}$ and multiply by $r$: $\\ rS_n=ar+ar^2+\\dots+ar^n$. Subtracting, almost every term cancels: $S_n-rS_n=a-ar^n$."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Sum of a GP","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"S_n=\\frac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}\\ \\ (\\text{neat when } r<1)\\qquad S_n=\\frac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}\\ \\ (\\text{neat when } r>1)"}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Sum to infinity","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"If $-1<r<1$, then $r^n$ gets closer and closer to 0 as $n$ grows, so $S_n$ gets closer to $\\dfrac{a}{1-r}$. The series **converges**."},{"k":"math","tex":"S_\\infty=\\frac{a}{1-r}\\qquad(|r|<1)"},{"k":"fig","id":"w16-halves","caption":"$\\tfrac12+\\tfrac14+\\tfrac18+\\dots$ fills a whole square."},{"k":"p","text":"If $|r|\\ge1$ the terms do not shrink, the sums grow without limit (or swing about), and there is **no** sum to infinity: the series **diverges**."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Recurring decimals","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A recurring decimal is an infinite GP: $\\ 0.\\overline{3}=0.3+0.03+0.003+\\dots=\\dfrac{0.3}{1-0.1}=\\dfrac13$."}]}],"figs":["w16-halves"]}],"examples":[{"title":"AP, GP or neither?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Decide whether each sequence is arithmetic or geometric and find the given term. (a) 11th term of $5,3,1,-1,\\dots$ (b) 23rd term of $0.1,0.15,0.2,\\dots$ (c) 6th term of $25,75,225,\\dots$ (d) 22nd term of $-2,-5,-8,\\dots$"}],"steps":["(a) Differences $-2$: AP. $\\ U_{11}=5+10(-2)=-15$.","(b) Differences $0.05$: AP. $\\ U_{23}=0.1+22(0.05)=1.2$.","(c) Ratios 3: GP. $\\ U_6=25\\times3^5=6075$.","(d) Differences $-3$: AP. $\\ U_{22}=-2+21(-3)=-65$."],"answer":"(a) $-15$ (b) 1.2 (c) 6075 (d) $-65$","figs":[]},{"title":"Finding terms of a GP","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Find (a) the 8th term of $2,6,18,54,\\dots$ (b) the 8th term of $96,48,24,\\dots$ (c) the 7th term of $2,-6,18,\\dots$"}],"steps":["(a) $a=2$, $r=3$: $\\ U_8=2\\times3^7=2\\times2187=4374$.","(b) $a=96$, $r=\\tfrac12$: $\\ U_8=96\\times\\left(\\tfrac12\\right)^7=\\tfrac{96}{128}=0.75$.","(c) $a=2$, $r=-3$: $\\ U_7=2\\times(-3)^6=1458$."],"answer":"(a) 4374 (b) 0.75 (c) 1458","figs":[]},{"title":"A GP from two terms","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The second and fourth terms of a GP are 9 and 4. Find the possible sequences."}],"steps":["$ar=9$ and $ar^3=4$. Divide: $r^2=\\tfrac49$, so $r=\\tfrac23$ or $r=-\\tfrac23$.","If $r=\\tfrac23$: $a=9\\div\\tfrac23=13.5$, giving $13.5,\\ 9,\\ 6,\\ 4,\\ \\dots$","If $r=-\\tfrac23$: $a=-13.5$, giving $-13.5,\\ 9,\\ -6,\\ 4,\\ \\dots$"],"answer":"$13.5, 9, 6, 4, \\dots$ or $-13.5, 9, -6, 4, \\dots$","figs":[]},{"title":"How many terms?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"How many terms are there in (a) $2,4,8,\\dots,128$ (b) $3,6,12,\\dots,3072$?"}],"steps":["(a) $2\\times2^{n-1}=128$, so $2^{n-1}=64=2^6$ and $n=7$.","(b) $3\\times2^{n-1}=3072$, so $2^{n-1}=1024=2^{10}$ and $n=11$.","With logarithms: $n-1=\\dfrac{\\log1024}{\\log2}=10$ ✓."],"answer":"(a) 7 (b) 11","figs":[]},{"title":"The geometric mean","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The numbers $x-2$, $x+1$ and $2x+2$ are consecutive terms of a GP. Find $x$ and the common ratio."}],"steps":["Middle term squared $=$ product of the outer terms: $(x+1)^2=(x-2)(2x+2)$.","$x^2+2x+1=2x^2-2x-4$, so $x^2-4x-5=0$ and $(x-5)(x+1)=0$.","$x=5$ gives $3,\\ 6,\\ 12$ with $r=2$. $\\ x=-1$ gives $-3,\\ 0,\\ 0$, which has no common ratio, so reject it."],"answer":"$x=5$, $r=2$","figs":[]},{"title":"Sums of GPs","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Find (a) the sum of the first 7 terms of $\\tfrac12,1,2,4,\\dots$ (b) $2+6+18+\\dots$ to 6 terms (c) the sum of the first 5 terms of the GP with $a=3$, $r=2$."}],"steps":["(a) $r=2$: $\\ S_7=\\dfrac{\\tfrac12(2^7-1)}{2-1}=\\tfrac12(127)=63.5$.","(b) $r=3$: $\\ S_6=\\dfrac{2(3^6-1)}{3-1}=729-1=728$.","(c) $S_5=\\dfrac{3(2^5-1)}{1}=93$."],"answer":"(a) 63.5 (b) 728 (c) 93","figs":[]},{"title":"Sums to infinity","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Find $\\tfrac12+\\tfrac14+\\tfrac18+\\tfrac1{16}+\\dots$ (b) Write $0.\\overline{27}=0.272727\\ldots$ as a fraction."}],"steps":["(a) $a=\\tfrac12$, $r=\\tfrac12$, $|r|<1$: $\\ S_\\infty=\\dfrac{1/2}{1-1/2}=1$ (see the square in the notes).","(b) $0.\\overline{27}=0.27+0.0027+\\dots$, a GP with $a=0.27$, $r=0.01$.","$S_\\infty=\\dfrac{0.27}{0.99}=\\dfrac{27}{99}=\\dfrac{3}{11}$."],"answer":"(a) 1 (b) $\\tfrac{3}{11}$","figs":[]},{"title":"A bouncing ball","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A ball is dropped from 10 m. Each bounce rises to $\\tfrac35$ of the height before. Find the height of the 4th bounce and the total distance the ball travels before it comes to rest."},{"k":"fig","id":"w16-bounce","caption":"The bounce heights form a GP with ratio 0.6."}],"steps":["Bounce heights: $6,\\ 3.6,\\ 2.16,\\ 1.296,\\ \\dots$ ($a=6$, $r=0.6$), so the 4th bounce is 1.296 m.","The ball falls 10 m, then goes **up and down** each bounce height.","Total $=10+2\\times\\dfrac{6}{1-0.6}=10+2\\times15=40$ m."],"answer":"1.296 m; 40 m","figs":["w16-bounce"]},{"title":"When does the sum pass 35?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"How many terms of $4+3.6+3.24+\\dots$ are needed for the sum to exceed 35?"}],"steps":["$a=4$, $r=0.9$: $\\ S_n=\\dfrac{4(1-0.9^n)}{0.1}=40(1-0.9^n)$.","$40(1-0.9^n)>35$ gives $0.9^n<0.125$.","Take logs (log 0.9 is negative, so the inequality turns round): $n>\\dfrac{\\log0.125}{\\log0.9}\\approx19.7$.","So 20 terms are needed. Check: $S_{19}\\approx34.6$ and $S_{20}\\approx35.1$ ✓."],"answer":"20 terms","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Geometric progressions","items":["GP: multiply by the common ratio $r=\\dfrac{U_{n+1}}{U_n}$.","$U_n=ar^{n-1}$. Geometric mean: $b^2=ac$.","$S_n=\\dfrac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}=\\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$.","$S_\\infty=\\dfrac{a}{1-r}$ only when $|r|<1$.","Use logarithms to find $n$ when the power is Find $r$.","a":"$\\tfrac{5}{1-r}=20$: $r=\\tfrac34$"}],"theory":[{"q":"Derive the formula $S_n=\\dfrac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}$ for the sum of the first $n$ terms of a GP, and explain why it gives $S_\\infty=\\dfrac a{1-r}$ when $|r|<1$.","steps":["$S_n=a+ar+ar^2+\\dots+ar^{n-1}$ $rS_n=ar+ar^2+\\dots+ar^{n-1}+ar^n$","Subtracting, every term except $a$ and $ar^n$ cancels: $\\ S_n-rS_n=a-ar^n$, so $S_n(1-r)=a(1-r^n)$ and $S_n=\\frac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}\\quad(r\\ne1).$","If $|r|<1$, then $r^n\\to0$ as $n$ grows (for example $0.5^{10}\\approx0.001$), so $S_n\\to\\dfrac{a}{1-r}$."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"The 2nd, 4th and 8th terms of an AP with first term 2 and non-zero common difference $d$ are consecutive terms of a GP. Find $d$ and the common ratio of the GP.","steps":["The terms are $2+d$, $2+3d$, $2+7d$. For a GP, $(2+3d)^2=(2+d)(2+7d)$.","$4+12d+9d^2=4+16d+7d^2$, so $2d^2=4d$ and $d(d-2)=0$. Since $d\\ne0$, $d=2$.","The terms are 4, 8, 16: a GP with common ratio **2**."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Write $0.1\\overline{6}=0.1666\\ldots$ as a fraction by using an infinite GP.","steps":["$0.1\\overline{6}=0.1+0.06+0.006+0.0006+\\dots$","The part after 0.1 is a GP with $a=0.06$ and $r=0.1$: its sum is $\\dfrac{0.06}{0.9}=\\dfrac{1}{15}$.","So $0.1\\overline{6}=\\dfrac1{10}+\\dfrac1{15}=\\dfrac{3+2}{30}=\\dfrac16$. Check: $1\\div6=0.1666\\ldots$ ✓."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Explain the difference between an AP and a GP, using the graph of each against $n$. Give one real situation modelled by each.","steps":["In an **AP** the same amount is **added** each time, so $U_n=a+(n-1)d$ is linear in $n$ and the points lie on a straight line. Example: a salary that rises by a fixed GH₵1500 every year.","In a **GP** the terms are **multiplied** by the same factor, so $U_n=ar^{n-1}$ is exponential: the points lie on a curve that rises faster and faster if $r>1$ (growth) or falls towards 0 if $0<r<1$ (decay). Example: money earning compound interest, or the value of a car depreciating by 20% a year."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"A GP has positive terms. The sum of the first two terms is 15 and the sum to infinity is 27. Find the first term and the common ratio.","steps":["$a+ar=15$ and $\\dfrac{a}{1-r}=27$, so $a=27(1-r)$.","Substitute: $27(1-r)(1+r)=15$, so $1-r^2=\\tfrac{15}{27}=\\tfrac59$ and $r^2=\\tfrac49$.","The terms are positive, so $r=\\tfrac23$ and $a=27\\times\\tfrac13=9$. The series is $9+6+4+\\dots$, and indeed $9+6=15$ ✓."],"answer":"","model":null}],"checklist":["I can find the common ratio and the $n$th term of a GP.","I can tell APs, GPs and other sequences The **growth factor** is $r=1+\\tfrac{p}{100}$ for an increase of $p\\%$, and $r=1-\\tfrac{p}{100}$ for a decrease.","Use the **$n$th term** for the amount **in** a particular step, and the **sum** for the **total** over several steps."]}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Watch the counting","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"If a population starts at $P$ and grows by a factor $r$ each year, then after $n$ years it is $Pr^n$: the starting value is year 0, so \"after $n$ years\" is the term $U_{n+1}=ar^n$. (c) Is the soup ever all gone? After how many days is less than 1 gallon left?"}],"steps":["(a) Each day $\\tfrac34$ remains: 12, 9, 6.75, 5.0625, 3.796875 gallons.","(b) $A_n=16\\left(\\tfrac34\\right)^n$.","(c) $\\left(\\tfrac34\\right)^n$ is never 0, so in this model the soup is never completely gone, although it becomes tiny.","$16(0.75)^n<1$ gives $n>\\dfrac{\\log(1/16)}{\\log0.75}\\approx9.6$: after **10 days** less than 1 gallon is left."],"answer":"(b) $16(0.75)^n$ (c) never all gone; after 10 days","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Modelling with sequences","items":["Same amount each step: AP. Same percentage each step: GP with $r=1\\pm\\tfrac{p}{100}$.","\"In step $n$\": the term $U_n$. \"Altogether\": the sum $S_n$.","After $n$ years from a start value $P$: $Pr^n$.","Regular deposits with interest form a geometric series.","Doubling time $n=\\dfrac{\\log2}{\\log r}$; half-life $n=\\dfrac{\\log\\tfrac12}{\\log r}$."]}],"quiz":[{"q":"\"A salary rises by GH₵500 every year.\" This is modelled by","options":["an arithmetic progression","a geometric progression","neither","a sum to infinity"],"correct":0,"explain":"A fixed amount is added."},{"q":"\"A population grows by 4% a year.\" The common ratio is","options":["1.04","0.04","4","0.96"],"correct":0,"explain":"$1+\\tfrac{4}{100}$."},{"q":"A car loses 15% of its value each year. After 3 years it is worth","options":["GH₵2662","GH₵2600","GH₵2420","GH₵6000"],"correct":0,"explain":"$2000\\times1.1^3$."},{"q":"Row 1 has 20 seats and each row has 3 more. Starting from 50, after 5 hours there are","options":["1600","250","800","3200"],"correct":0,"explain":"$50\\times2^5$."},{"q":"The doubling time for growth of 7% a year is about","options":["10.2 years","7 years","14 years","2 years"],"correct":0,"explain":"$\\tfrac{\\log2}{\\log1.07}$."},{"q":"Which grows larger in the long run?","options":["any exponential growth with $r>1$","any linear growth","they always stay equal","it depends only on the first term"],"correct":0,"explain":"Exponential growth eventually overtakes linear growth."}],"exercise":[{"q":"After knee surgery you jog 12 minutes a day in week 1 and add 6 minutes a day each week. <script type="application/json" id="pack-y2w18">{"year":2,"week":18,"id":"y2w18","title":"Surface Area: Nets, Formulas and SI and Imperial Units","subtitle":"Surface area and why it matters; square units in the SI system (m², cm²) and the imperial system (ft², in²) and converting between them; nets of prisms, pyramids, cylinders and cones; formulas for the surface area of cubes, cuboids, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones and spheres; finding a missing dimension; composite solids; and checking answers.","family":"geometry","section":{"no":7,"name":"Surface Areas and Volumes","strand":"Geometry Around Us","from":18,"to":20},"outcomes":["Explain surface area and use nets to find the surface area of prisms and pyramids.","Convert areas between m² and cm², ft² and in², and between SI and imperial units.","Use formulas for the surface area of cylinders, cones and spheres, finding a slant height by Pythagoras.","Work backwards from a surface area to a missing length.","Solve real problems such as painting and packaging, and verify the answers."],"keywords":["surface area","net","face","lateral surface","curved surface","total surface area","square metre","square centimetre","square foot","square inch","SI unit","imperial unit","conversion factor","prism","pyramid","cylinder","cone","slant height","sphere","hemisphere","composite solid"],"notes":[{"title":"What is surface area?","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The **surface area** of a solid is the total area of all its faces and curved surfaces. If you open a box out flat, you get its **net**; the surface area is the area of the net."},{"k":"box","kind":"life","title":"Why it matters","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Surface area tells a painter how much paint to buy, a packaging company how much card a box needs, a tailor how much cloth covers a cushion, and a builder how many roofing sheets a roof needs."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Units of area","blocks":[{"k":"fig","id":"w18-units","caption":"Square units in the SI and imperial systems."},{"k":"table","head":["Conversion","Rule"],"rows":[["m² to cm²","$\\times10\\,000$ (because $1\\text{ m}=100\\text{ cm}$ and $100^2=10\\,000$)"],["ft² to in²","$\\times144$ (because $1\\text{ ft}=12\\text{ in}$ and $12^2=144$)"],["m² to ft²","$\\times10.7639$"],["ft² to m²","$\\times0.092903$ (or $\\div10.7639$)"],["in² to cm²","$\\times6.4516$ (because $1\\text{ in}=2.54\\text{ cm}$ and $2.54^2=6.4516$)"],["cm² to in²","$\\div6.4516$ (or $\\times0.155$)"]]},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Square the length factor","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"To convert **areas**, square the factor for lengths. Since $1\\text{ m}=100\\text{ cm}$, $1\\text{ m}^2$ is $100^2=10\\,000\\text{ cm}^2$, not 100."}]}],"figs":["w18-units"]},{"title":"Nets and surface area","blocks":[{"k":"fig","id":"w18-net","caption":"A cuboid and its net."},{"k":"p","text":"For any **prism** (a solid with the same cross-section all along its length):"},{"k":"math","tex":"\\text{SA}=2A+P\\times L"},{"k":"p","text":"where $A$ is the area of the cross-section, $P$ its perimeter and $L$ the length of the prism."},{"k":"p","text":"For a **pyramid**: surface area $=$ area of the base $+$ the areas of the triangular faces."}],"figs":["w18-net"]},{"title":"Formulas","blocks":[{"k":"table","head":["Solid","Total surface area"],"rows":[["cube, edge $a$","$6a^2$"],["cuboid $l\\times w\\times h$","$2(lw+wh+lh)$"],["cylinder, radius $r$, height $h$","$2\\pi r^2+2\\pi rh=2\\pi r(r+h)$"],["cone, radius $r$, slant height $l$","$\\pi r^2+\\pi rl=\\pi r(r+l)$"],["sphere, radius $r$","$4\\pi r^2$"],["solid hemisphere","$2\\pi r^2+\\pi r^2=3\\pi r^2$"]]},{"k":"fig","id":"w18-cylcone","caption":"Nets of a cylinder and a cone."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Slant height","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The slant height $l$ of a cone is not its vertical height $h$. They are linked by Pythagoras: $\\ l=\\sqrt{r^2+h^2}$. Find its surface area."},{"k":"fig","id":"w18-tri","caption":"The net of the triangular prism."}],"steps":["Two triangles: $2\\times\\tfrac12\\times5\\times4.3=21.5$ m².","Three rectangles, each $5\\times7=35$ m²: total 105 m².","Surface area $=21.5+105=126.5$ m².","Prism formula check: $2(10.75)+(5+5+5)\\times7=21.5+105$ ✓."],"answer":"126.5 m²","figs":["w18-tri"]},{"title":"Cylinder and cone","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Find the total surface area of a cylinder of radius 3.5 cm and height 6 cm $\\left(\\pi=\\tfrac{22}{7}\\right)$. The sector is the fraction $\\dfrac{2\\pi r}{2\\pi l}=\\dfrac rl$ of that circle, so its area is $\\frac rl\\times\\pi l^2=\\pi rl.$","Adding the circular base gives the total surface area $\\pi rl+\\pi r^2=\\pi r(r+l)$."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Show that the surface area of a regular hexagonal prism with base edge $a$ and length $h$ is $6ah+3\\sqrt3\\,a^2$. So the total is $6ah+3\\sqrt3\\,a^2$.","For $a=4$, $h=10$: $\\ 240+48\\sqrt3\\approx240+83.1=323.1$ cm²."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"A company packs a ball of radius 5 cm in a cube-shaped box that just fits around it. The ratio does not depend on the size of the ball."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Two similar cylinders have heights 6 cm and 9 cm. The smaller has total surface area 120 cm². Hence, using $1\\text{ m}\\approx3.2808$ ft, show that $1\\text{ m}^3\\approx35.31\\text{ ft}^3$.","steps":["$1\\text{ m}=100$ cm, so $1\\text{ m}^3=100\\times100\\times100=1\\,000\\,000$ cm³. Since $1\\text{ L}=1000$ cm³, this is $1\\,000\\,000\\div1000=1000$ L.","$1\\text{ ft}=12$ in, so $1\\text{ ft}^3=12^3=1728$ in³.","$1\\text{ m}^3=(3.2808\\text{ ft})^3=3.2808^3\\text{ ft}^3\\approx35.31$ ft³. Lengths convert by the factor, areas by its square, volumes by its cube."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"An ice cream is a cone of radius 3 cm and height 10 cm, filled level and topped with a hemisphere of radius 3 cm. Find the total volume of ice cream.","steps":["Cone: $\\tfrac13\\pi(3^2)(10)=30\\pi$ cm³.","Hemisphere: $\\tfrac23\\pi(3^3)=18\\pi$ cm³.","Total $=48\\pi\\approx150.8$ cm³."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"A bucket is a frustum (a cone with its tip cut off). Its top radius is 15 cm, its base radius is 10 cm and its depth is 24 cm. Find its capacity in litres.","steps":["Extend the sides to make a full cone of height $H$. By similar triangles, $\\dfrac{15}{H}=\\dfrac{10}{H-24}$, so $15H-360=10H$ and $H=72$ cm. The small cone removed has height 48 cm. $V=\\tfrac13\\pi(15^2)(72)-\\tfrac13\\pi(10^2)(48)=5400\\pi-1600\\pi=3800\\pi$","$3800\\pi\\approx11\\,938$ cm³, so the bucket holds about **11.9 litres**."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Two similar water jugs have heights 10 cm and 15 cm. The smaller holds 0.8 L. How much does the larger hold? Explain why.","steps":["The scale factor for lengths is $k=\\dfrac{15}{10}=1.5$.","Volume is length $\\times$ length $\\times$ length, so volumes are multiplied by $k^3=3.375$.","The larger jug holds $0.8\\times3.375=2.7$ L."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"A lead pipe is a hollow cylinder 2 m long, with outer radius 3 cm and inner radius 2.5 cm. (a) Find the volume of lead. (b) Lead has a density of 11.3 g per cm³. Find the mass of the pipe in kg.","steps":["(a) Length $=200$ cm. Volume $=\\pi(3^2-2.5^2)(200)=\\pi(2.75)(200)=550\\pi\\approx1727.9$ cm³.","(b) Mass $=1727.9\\times11.3\\approx19\\,525$ g, about **19.5 kg**."],"answer":"","model":null}],"checklist":["I can explain the difference between volume and capacity.","I can convert between cm³, m³, mL and L.","I can convert volumes between SI and imperial units.","I can find volumes of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres.","I can find a missing dimension from a volume.","I can find volumes of composite and recast solids."],"plan":{"lessons":[[{"j":0,"notes":true,"exs":[]},{"j":1,"notes":true,"exs":[]},{"j":2,"notes":true,"exs":[]},{"j":3,"notes":true,"exs":[0]},{"j":4,"notes":true,"exs":[1]}],[{"j":4,"notes":false,"exs":[2,3,4,5,6,7,8]}]],"exSec":[3,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4],"quizSec":[1,3,2,4,4,4,4,3,4,4],"exerSec":[3,3,4,4,4,4,4,4,0,2],"thSec":[3,4,0,0,0],"sumSec":[0,0,4,4],"chkSec":[0,3,2,4,0,4],"weights":[529.7,679.85,380.1,1362.05,6828.85],"figs":[{"id":"w19-litre","sec":1,"lesson":1,"caption":"A litre is a 10 cm cube; a thousand of them fill a cubic metre."},{"id":"w19-composite","sec":4,"lesson":2,"ex":4,"caption":"A cuboid topped by a pyramid."}]},"next":"Volume and Capacity in the Real World","tm":{"sectionNo":7,"sectionName":"Surface Areas and Volumes","strand":"Geometry Around Us","sub":"Measurement","cs":["Demonstrate conceptual understanding of the measurement of surface area, volume and capacity of solid shapes."],"lo":["Determine the volume and capacity of solid shapes and solve problems that involve SI and imperial units in surface area, volume and capacity measurements."],"indicators":["Solve problems that involve SI and imperial units in volume/capacity measurements."],"focal":["Measurements of volume and capacity"],"exemplars":["Collaborative learning: Learners discuss and solve problems that involve the volume of 3-D objects and composite 3-D objects using formulas.
